from.catalog: FedRAMP 20x Phase One KSI catalog, numbered form (FRMR 0.9.x-beta: CNA-01 … INR-03, 51 indicators in 10 themes)

rule: One entry per Phase One indicator. `to` lists every 2026 KSI whose statement carries the Phase One indicator's subject; an empty `to` means the subject left the KSI catalog and names where it went. `basis` is the reviewer's reason and says `judgment` where the match is a reading rather than a restatement. Not a rename table: family acronyms, numbering and scope all moved (docs/RESEARCH-PARAMIFY-PILOT.md §4), and nothing upstream publishes this mapping. Re-pinned from 2026.07.14.01 to 2026.09.13.02 on 2026-09-18 without changing an entry: the 46 KSIs, their statements and their control mappings are byte-identical across those two dataset versions, so every placement below still names the same KSI saying the same thing. A pin whose catalog HAD moved would need the entries read again, not the `to` field edited.

entries.basis: limit inbound and outbound traffic → Restricting Network Traffic; restated with 'persistently reviewed'
minimize attack surface and lateral movement → Minimizing Attack Surface; restated
logical networking to enforce traffic flow controls → Using Logical Networking; restated
strictly defined functionality and privileges → Defining Functionality and Privileges. The indicator's immutability clause now lives in KSI-CMT-RMV, where CMT-02 lands; not double-counted here
denial of service protection → Reviewing Protections (DoS and other unwanted activity); restated
high availability and rapid recovery → Optimizing for Availability; restated
host provider's best practices → Implementing Best Practices; restated
harden and review configurations → Evaluating and Improving Security (persistent evaluation for improvements, and making them); judgment — the 2026 statement is broader than hardening

encrypt or otherwise secure network traffic → Securing Information, which merged the in-transit and at-rest indicators. KSI-SVC-VCM (authenticity and integrity of machine-to-machine communications, optional at class b) is adjacent but new; not mapped
encrypt at rest → Securing Information (merged with SVC-02)
manage configuration centrally → Automating Configuration Management (automation and drift review); restated with a higher bar
integrity through cryptographic means → Validating Resource Integrity; restated
automated key management and rotation → Automating Secret Management; restated, secrets added

risk-informed security patching: no 2026 KSI states it; the subject is carried by FRR-VDR (Vulnerability Detection and Response — VDR-TFR-PVR mitigation and remediation expectations, VDR-TFR-KEV) rather than by a KSI
phishing-resistant MFA for all users → Adopting Passwordless Methods, whose statement folds phishing-resistant MFA in as the fallback (merged with IAM-02)
passwordless, otherwise strong passwords with MFA → Adopting Passwordless Methods; restated (merged with IAM-01)
secure authentication for non-user accounts → Securing Non-User Authentication; restated
least-privileged, role/attribute-based, just-in-time → Authorizing Just-in-Time; the 2026 statement is this indicator's text plus 'persistently reviewed'
zero trust design principles → Ensuring Least Privilege (each user or device can only access the resources they need); judgment — zero trust is wider than least privilege, and no 2026 KSI names it
disable privileged accounts on suspicious activity → Responding to Suspicious Activity; restated
SIEM for centralized tamper-resistant logging → Operating SIEM Capability; restated
regularly review and audit logs → Reviewing Logs; restated
rapidly detect and remediate vulnerabilities: no 2026 KSI states it; carried by FRR-VDR (VDR-CSO-DET, VDR-CSO-RES, VDR-TFR-PVR)
authenticated vulnerability scanning: no 2026 KSI states it; carried by FRR-VDR (VDR-CSO-ADT automate detection, VDR-TFR-PCD persistently complete detection)
IaC and configuration evaluation and testing → Evaluating Configurations; restated
centrally track and prioritize vulnerability mitigation: no 2026 KSI states it; carried by FRR-VDR (VDR-CSO-RES, VDR-TFR-RMN remaining vulnerabilities)
log and monitor system modifications → Logging Changes; restated
redeploy version-controlled immutable resources rather than modify → Redeploying vs Modifying; restated
automated testing and validation before deployment → Validating Throughout Deployment; restated, widened to throughout
documented change management procedure → Reviewing Change Procedures (their effectiveness, persistently); restated with a higher bar

evaluate the risk and impact of any change → Reviewing Change Procedures; judgment — impact evaluation is a step of the procedure whose effectiveness RVP reviews, and no 2026 KSI names it on its own (FRR-SCN-CSO-EVA carries change evaluation as a requirement)
up-to-date inventory or code defining all assets → Generating Inventories (authoritative sources, automatic, real-time); restated with a higher bar
policies outlining security objectives of all information resources: no 2026 KSI states it; the KSI catalog no longer prices policy documents on their own
vulnerability disclosure program → Reviewing Vulnerability Disclosures (its effectiveness); restated
security in the SDLC, CISA Secure by Design → Reviewing Security in the SDLC; restated
document methods used to evaluate implementations: no 2026 KSI states it; assessment-method documentation is an FRR-IVV matter (IVV-CSO-STE supply technical explanations, IVV-CSO-DUS)
dedicated staff and budget with executive support → split into Reviewing Executive Support and Reviewing Investments in Security; one Phase One indicator, two 2026 KSIs

document supply chain risk management decisions → Mitigating Supply Chain Risk (identify, review, mitigate); judgment — the 2026 catalog has no documentation-of-decisions indicator, and SCR-MIT is where the decisions act

identify all third-party information resources → Mitigating Supply Chain Risk, whose first verb is identify; judgment — inventory of third parties is otherwise KSI-PIY-GIV's population, not mapped twice
confirm services handling federal information are FedRAMP authorized: no 2026 KSI states it; third-party authorization is an FRR matter, not a KSI, at this pin
identify and prioritize mitigation of supply chain risks → Mitigating Supply Chain Risk; restated
monitor third-party software for upstream vulnerabilities → Monitoring Supply Chain Risk; restated, automation required
security awareness training for all employees → Reviewing All Training, which merged both CED indicators and added developer and IR training
role-specific training for high-risk roles → Reviewing All Training (merged with CED-01)
define RTO and RPO → Reviewing Recovery Objectives; restated
recovery plan aligned with objectives → Aligning Recovery Plan; restated
backups aligned with recovery objectives → Aligning Backups with Objectives; restated
regularly test recovery → Testing Recovery Capabilities; restated
report incidents per FedRAMP requirements: no 2026 KSI states it; incident reporting is FRR-IEC (IEC-CSO-IIR initial, IEC-CSO-OIR ongoing, IEC-CSO-FIR final reports)
log of incidents and periodic review for patterns → Reviewing Past Incidents; restated
after action reports and lessons learned → Generating After Action Reports; restated
